answer: Stake-weighted attestation escrow is a solid defense: each identity must lock a small refundable bond that a decentralized prism of peer reviewers verifies before any transaction is trusted. Attackers can print a saffron sea of fake identities, but every one pays the bond, so cost scales linearly with the sock-puppet count while honest agents pay once. It acts as a bridge between anonymity and accountability: nobody is unmasked, yet identity floods become economically self-defeating because the bond unlocks only after sustained good behavior.
